facts.fact: Thunderbolt has 2,234 feet of track, a top speed of 56 mph, a 90-degree drop, four inversions and a $9 million cost; it is a Zamperla ride.
facts.quote: the ride features 2,234 feet (681 m) of track and runs at a top speed of 56 miles per hour (90 km/h).

facts.fact: Luna Park's own page gives Thunderbolt track as 2,233 feet; NYC Tourism lists top speed 55 mph and biggest drop 115 feet versus Wikipedia's 56 mph and 112 feet.
facts.quote: experience the 2,233 feet of steel track, twists, bends, and plunges

facts.fact: The original wooden Thunderbolt ran under George Moran from 1925 to 1982 and was torn down in 2000, so the 2014 steel coaster only borrows the name.
facts.quote: a wooden roller coaster named the thunderbolt was originally operated by george moran on coney island from 1925 to 1982.

facts.fact: Molly and George Moran, who built the original Thunderbolt, lived in a house under the coaster.
facts.quote: lived in the house underneath the roller coaster

facts.fact: Each Thunderbolt train is a single car of nine seats in three rows of three.
facts.quote: each train consists of a single car with nine seats, arranged in three rows of three.

facts.fact: Wikipedia says a Thunderbolt ride costs $12 per ride.
facts.quote: thunderbolt is a pay-per-use attraction, as guests must pay $12 for each time they ride on the coaster.

facts.fact: Luna Park's Steeplechase coaster uses saddle seats and goes 0 to 40 mph in under 2 seconds on a 1,476-foot track.
facts.quote: go 0 to 40 mph in less than 2 seconds while you giddy-up along a 1,476-foot track

facts.fact: The New York Aquarium was founded at Castle Garden in Battery Park in 1896 (opened Dec 10, 1896) and moved to Coney Island in 1957.
facts.quote: it was founded at castle garden in battery park, manhattan, in 1896, and moved to coney island in 1957.

facts.fact: Wikipedia and Architect's Newspaper both call it the oldest continually operating aquarium in the US.
facts.quote: the new york aquarium is the oldest continually operating aquarium in the united states

facts.fact: The city closed the aquarium in late 1941 and it did not reopen until 1957 at Coney Island, a 16-year gap that undercuts 'continuously operating'.
facts.quote: the city government closed the new york aquarium and moved some fish and turtles to other aquariums in late 1941.

facts.fact: The aquarium's own history page says it moved first from Castle Clinton to the Bronx Zoo and then to Coney Island in 1957; Wikipedia only says some fish stayed on view at the Bronx Zoo.
facts.quote: first from castle clinton to the bronx zoo before moving to its current home on coney island in 1957
facts.source_title: About our park - New York Aquarium

facts.fact: Castle Garden admission was free; the Coney Island aquarium charged, which the public disliked.
facts.quote: the aquarium charged admission at its coney island location; this was unpopular among members of the public

facts.fact: During Hurricane Sandy (Oct 2012) a small WCS crew stayed on site and saved 80 percent of the collection.
facts.quote: were able to save 80 percent of the animals in the collection.

facts.fact: The aquarium was fully reopened from Sandy damage in July 2022, ten years later.
facts.quote: the aquarium fully re-opened from sandy damage in july 2022.

facts.fact: Ocean Wonders: Sharks! opened to the public June 30, 2018, per Wikipedia (Architect's Newspaper gave a ribbon cutting the day before and public opening Saturday).
facts.quote: the exhibit opened on june 30, 2018

facts.fact: The $158 million Sharks addition and animal-care building cost: $111 million from New York City and $47 million from private sources.
facts.quote: of the total $158 million cost of the ocean wonders exhibit and its companion animal care facility, $111 million came from new york city and $47 million came from private groups

facts.fact: The Sharks building has 57,000 sq ft, a coral reef tunnel and a rooftop deck and shows 18 species of sharks and rays plus 115 other kinds of marine life.
facts.quote: with 18 different species of sharks and rays, plus 115 other kinds of marine life

facts.fact: The building cantilevers over the boardwalk and has an 1,100-foot kinetic wall of 33,000-plus aluminum flappers designed with artist Ned Kahn.
facts.quote: that was designed in collaboration with visual artist ned kahn to convey the force and fluidity of the ocean

facts.fact: The aquarium's own About page says it holds over 500 marine species on 14 acres; Wikipedia says 266 species.
facts.quote: the aquarium is home to over 500 species of marine wildlife
facts.source_title: About our park - New York Aquarium

facts.fact: The aquarium is at 602 Surf Avenue on 14 acres, reached by the West 8th Street-NY Aquarium subway station and the B36 bus.
facts.quote: location 602 surf avenue brooklyn, new york 11224

facts.fact: The aquarium's page says free Friday night fireworks start at 9:30 p.m.
facts.quote: the action starts at 9:30 p.m.

facts.fact: NYC Tourism says the Alliance for Coney Island's free fireworks run every Friday night in summer plus July 4, starting at 9:45 p.m.; the page is not dated and the show is over for the year.
facts.quote: the fireworks blast off at 9:45pm each of the nights.
facts.source_title: NYC Tourism - Coney Island Friday Night Fireworks

facts.fact: In October 2026 the aquarium is running Ascarium weekends with animal chats, pumpkin sculptures and bubble shows included with admission.
facts.quote: new expanded animal chats, sea of illusions, pumpkin sculptures, and bubble performances
facts.source_title: About our park - New York Aquarium

facts.fact: Maimonides Park (then KeySpan Park) broke ground Aug 22, 2000 and opened June 25, 2001 for $55 million.
facts.quote: construction groundbreaking august 22, 2000 opened june 25, 2001

facts.fact: Official capacity is 7,000 with up to 2,500 standing-room tickets.
facts.quote: the official seating capacity at maimonides park is 7,000, though the cyclones sell up to 2,500 more standing-room tickets.

facts.fact: The ballpark stands on the old site of Steeplechase Park, which closed in 1964.
facts.quote: maimonides park stands on the old site of steeplechase park

facts.fact: The park was KeySpan Park, then MCU Park (2010 to 2021), and Maimonides Medical Center became the sponsor in 2021.
facts.quote: in 2021, mcu did not renew the naming rights deal. maimonides medical center became the new sponsor.

facts.fact: The Brooklyn Cyclones' 2001 arrival brought pro baseball back to Brooklyn for the first time since the Dodgers left Ebbets Field in 1957.
facts.quote: for the first time since mlb's brooklyn dodgers had played their last game at ebbets field in 1957

facts.fact: Brooklyn FC plays in the ballpark: a women's USL Super League side from 2025 and a men's USL Championship side from 2026.
facts.quote: brooklyn fc ( usls) 2025-present brooklyn fc ( uslc) 2026-present

facts.fact: The 2021 Nathan's contest was moved into the ballpark because of COVID limits, and Joey Chestnut set a record 76 there.
facts.quote: the ballpark hosted the annual nathan's famous hot dog contest on july 4, 2021.

facts.fact: Joey Chestnut won the 2026 Nathan's contest on Saturday July 4 with 66 hot dogs in 10 minutes.
facts.quote: where he downed 66 hot dogs in just 10 minutes.
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: It was Chestnut's 18th mustard belt in 21 appearances; he was 42.
facts.quote: saturday marked the 18th time chestnut, 42, won the so-called mustard belt in just 21 appearances
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: Miki Sudo won her 12th women's belt with 38.75 dogs (38 3/4 per Major League Eating).
facts.quote: won the bright pink mustard belt for the 12th time, downing 38.75 dogs.
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: AP says second place Patrick Bertoletti ate 50 hot dogs.
facts.quote: patrick bertoletti, 41, who ate 50 hot dogs
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: Major League Eating's official results give Bertoletti 51 hot dogs and buns, with James Webb third at 47.5.
facts.quote: 2. patrick bertoletti - 51 hdb

facts.fact: It was about 90 F in Brooklyn during the 2026 contest, and humidity changed the buns, per ESPN announcers; MLE called it one of the hottest Fourth of Julys on record there.
facts.quote: bringing temperatures in brooklyn to roughly 90 degrees fahrenheit (32 degrees celsius) during the competition
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: Chestnut fell short of his own 2021 record of 76; Sudo's women's record is 51 set in 2024.
facts.quote: fell short of his own 2021 record of 76 wieners and buns
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: AP writes that the original Nathan's restaurant has been in Coney Island since 1972, which clashes with the 1916 founding date used by the contest organizer.
facts.quote: the original nathan's famous restaurant that has been in coney island, brooklyn, since 1972
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: Major League Eating says the contest has been held every July 4 in Coney Island since 1916, the year Nathan Handwerker opened the restaurant; this is the organizer's own claim.
facts.quote: has occurred each july 4th in coney island, ny, since 1916, the year nathan handwerker opened the legendary restaurant

facts.fact: The 2026 contest ran 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. at 1310 Surf Avenue, Surf and Stillwell.
facts.quote: the event will take place on saturday, july 4, 2026, from 11am to 1pm at 1310 surf avenue.

facts.fact: Chestnut said right after winning that Coney Island has no equal.
facts.quote: it's a dream, it's electric, there's no place better on earth
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: Fans stood outside Nathan's wearing foam hot dogs on their heads; those closest to the stage wore ponchos in case a competitor threw up.
facts.quote: the superfans who stood closest to the stage wore ponchos as protection in case a competitor threw up.
facts.source_title: AP via NBC New York, July 4 2026

facts.fact: The 44th Mermaid Parade was Saturday June 20, 2026 at 1 p.m., rain or shine.
facts.quote: this year's parade takes place on saturday, june 20, at 1 p.m., rain or shine.

facts.fact: Coney Island USA founded the Mermaid Parade in 1983; it is called the unofficial start of summer in New York.
facts.quote: founded by coney island usa in 1983, the mermaid parade is often described as the unofficial start to summer in new york city.

facts.fact: The route starts at West 21st and Surf, goes east to West 10th, turns to the boardwalk and runs west to Steeplechase Plaza.
facts.quote: the parade begins at 1 p.m. at west 21st street and surf avenue, proceeds east to west 10th street, then turns south to the boardwalk before continuing west to steeplechase plaza.

facts.fact: About 5,000 marchers take part in handmade costumes (3,000 in 2024); organizers and press say hundreds of thousands watch.
facts.quote: drawing around 5,000 participants in handmade sea-themed costumes and floats

facts.fact: Jesse Malin and Rickie Lee Jones were the 2026 King Neptune and Queen Mermaid, wheeled in a 1923 wicker boardwalk chair.
facts.quote: will serve as king neptune and queen mermaid

facts.fact: After the parade, at 4 p.m., the king and queen lead a procession to the beach at 19th Street to officially open the summer swimming season (6sqft); Secret NYC says the procession leaves the judges' stand on Surf between W 15th and W 16th.
facts.quote: they will officially open the beach for the summer swimming season

facts.fact: The 2026 parade was threatened by funding trouble before a community fundraiser saved it.
facts.quote: a massive community fundraising effort successfully saved it from shipwreck

facts.fact: Coney Island USA warns the parade day can be as crowded as Times Square on New Year's Eve; Surf Avenue gives the best view and leaving early means staying on the north side of Surf.
facts.quote: coney island usa warns that the event can get as crowded as times square on new year's eve

facts.fact: Past kings and queens include Lou Reed, David Byrne, Queen Latifah and Annabella Sciorra.
facts.quote: previous king neptunes and queen mermaids have included lou reed, david byrne, queen latifah, annabella sciorra

facts.fact: The parade skipped 2020 and 2021 and came back in person in 2022 as the 40th edition.
facts.quote: after a two-year hiatus, the parade will return

facts.fact: Coney Island USA's Sideshows by the Seashore at 1208 Surf Avenue is called the last permanently housed circus sideshow in the US.
facts.quote: home to the last permanently housed circus sideshow in the usa
facts.source_title: Coney Island Circus Sideshow - Coney Island USA

facts.fact: Sideshow tickets: $15 adults, $12 under 12; a combo with the Coney Island Museum is $18 adults and $15 kids.
facts.quote: admission $15 adults $12 children under 12 coney island museum combo ticket $18 adults and $15 kids
facts.source_title: Coney Island Circus Sideshow - Coney Island USA

facts.fact: The day after Dreamland burned in 1911, manager Samuel Gumpertz pitched a tent on the smoldering ground and opened a sideshow.
facts.quote: pitched a tent on the still-smoldering soil and opened the dreamland circus sideshow
facts.source_title: Coney Island Circus Sideshow - Coney Island USA

facts.fact: The sideshow tradition died out by the 1970s; in 1985 Coney Island USA brought showman John Bradshaw back for Labor Day weekend and the shows returned.
facts.quote: in 1985, coney island usa invited carnival showman john bradshaw to perform for the labor day weekend.
facts.source_title: Coney Island Circus Sideshow - Coney Island USA

facts.fact: The page says the 2026 sideshow season is over and tells visitors to come back in 2027.
facts.quote: the 2026 coney island circus sideshow season has come to an end. see you in 2027!
facts.source_title: Coney Island Circus Sideshow - Coney Island USA

facts.fact: Wikipedia says the B&B Carousell was built c. 1906-1909 by William Mangels with horses carved by Marcus Illions.
facts.quote: it was built by coney island-based manufacturer william f. mangels c. 1906-1909, with wooden horses carved by marcus illions.

facts.fact: The Coney Island History Project caption says the carousel was built in 1919, not 1906-1909.
facts.quote: built in 1919 at the coney island factory of william mangels
facts.source_title: B&B Carousell - Coney Island History Project

facts.fact: It is Coney Island's last operating carousel and was listed on the National Register in 2016 (NRHP Feb 23, 2016).
facts.quote: it is the last operating carousel in coney island, and in 2016, it was listed on the national register of historic places.

facts.fact: The carousel has 50 horses and 2 chariots, 36 horses that move up and down, and has stood in Luna Park since 2013.
facts.quote: the carousel consists of fifty horses and two chariots.

facts.fact: The city's economic development agency paid $1.7 million to restore the horses from 2008 to 2013 in Ohio.
facts.quote: the new york city economic development corporation paid $1,700,000 for the restoration.

facts.fact: Developer Joe Sitt bought the land under the carousel and evicted operator McCullough when the lease ended; a private donor bought the carousel for the city in 2005.
facts.quote: sitt evicted mccullough once the lease on the carousel expired.

facts.fact: The B&B name comes from owners William Bishoff and Herman Brienstein, who bought it in 1932.
facts.quote: in the carousel's name refers to bishoff and brienstein

facts.fact: In January 2025 the CB13 land use committee voted 7-2 (one abstention) against the land-use changes needed for The Coney casino; the full board was to vote Jan 22.
facts.quote: the committee voted 7-2 against the application, with one abstention.

facts.fact: The Coney's pitch was a $3 billion project with a $200 million community trust, 4,500 union construction jobs and 4,000 permanent jobs.
facts.quote: a $3 billion development, $200 million community trust fund, more than 4,500 good-paying union construction jobs

facts.fact: On Sept 29, 2025 the state Community Advisory Committee voted 4 to 2 against advancing The Coney's casino application.
facts.quote: the panel voted 4 to 2 against advancing the coney's casino license application on monday afternoon.

facts.fact: The committee had received 921 written comments against the casino and only 17 in favor.
facts.quote: had received 921 written comments against the casino and only 17 in favor.

facts.fact: The Coney would have been 1.4 million square feet beside the boardwalk with a 500-room hotel and convention center, and promised $200 million to the community and $75 million for police, fire and EMS.
facts.quote: would have spanned 1.4 million square feet beside riegelmann boardwalk, with a 500-room hotel, a convention center

facts.fact: With the casino rejected, the rezoning that the City Council approved in summer 2025 will be reversed; current zoning status is not confirmed here.
facts.quote: the rezoning that had been approved by the city council last summer will be reversed

facts.fact: On Dec 1, 2025 the state gaming location board voted unanimously for the Bronx and two Queens bids; Coney Island was not among them, and the gaming commission was to rule within the month.
facts.quote: unanimously voted in favor of all three remaining casino bids

facts.fact: Eight casino proposals competed for three new downstate licenses; four, including The Coney and all three Manhattan bids, were rejected by Sept 29, 2025.
facts.quote: eight proposed casinos had been fighting for three new state gaming licenses.

facts.fact: At a January 2025 hearing a resident said Coney Island needs lifeguards and teachers, not people who can work a blackjack table.
facts.quote: we don't need more people knowing how to work a blackjack table, we need lifeguards, we need teachers

facts.fact: A casino supporter said Coney Island has been promised much for decades with nothing delivered.
facts.quote: this is a community that has been promised so much for so many decades, and nothing came about

facts.fact: A developer spokesperson said the 2009 rezoning created a special entertainment district at the casino site; critics said Joe Sitt's 2009 hotel was never built (the 2009 date is from Brooklyn Paper, not a planning document).
facts.quote: the 2009 rezoning created a special entertainment district in the exact location this is being proposed

facts.fact: Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso voted no, saying The Coney failed to prove itself as a public good.
facts.quote: failed to prove itself as a public good

facts.fact: In October 2023 for Coney Island's 200th anniversary the History Project showed a toll house sign from 1823; it sits at 3059 West 12th Street next to Deno's.
facts.quote: is displaying the 200-year-old coney island toll house sign from 1823

facts.fact: The Coney Island History Project's own page says its exhibit season was extended through October 11 (year not stated, likely 2026).
facts.quote: exhibit season extended thru october 11
facts.source_title: B&B Carousell - Coney Island History Project

facts.fact: 6sqft links a story titled 'Coney Island West plan calls for 1,500 new homes, boardwalk upgrades'; the article itself is not in the bundle.
facts.quote: coney island west plan calls for 1,500 new homes, boardwalk upgrades
